description:
We are Team THARA (Amman 2026), tackling climate and agricultural challenges in Jordan by using NASA Earth observation data to build smart, data-driven irrigation & farming tools. Based in Amman, we blend tech with natural impact.

We’re looking for passionate minds in:

• AI / ML & Data Analysis

• Software / Web Dev & UI/UX

• Earth Science / Agriculture

Join THARA to build solutions that touch the earth and empower local farmers! Let's innovate together.
summary:
THARA helps open-field vegetable growers compare crops and planting dates against the days and quantities of water they expect to receive. The Arabic and English web app uses NASA POWER daily temperatures from 2015 through 2024 and published FAO-56 methods to estimate crop water use. Growers can compare up to three scenarios, change a date or irrigation turn, trace the calculation to its source data, and save a printable plan.

A separate Deir Alla forage case compares an unknown farm baseline with two sequences documented in local research: sorghum followed by vetch and sesbania followed by barley. Priorities bring the most relevant questions forward without ranking the strategies.

THARA makes seasonal tradeoffs and missing information easier to see. The weather is historical, and the estimates still need local calibration and testing with growers.
details:
THARA explores a decision at the center of Field Shift: how a grower can compare the next crop and planting date under a recurring irrigation schedule. The grower selects a location, enters the field area, previous crop and water turns, and compares up to three crop and planting-date scenarios. Turn volume can be entered directly or calculated from flow and duration. The fictional Deir Alla example opens with authentic saved NASA data.

NASA POWER Daily Point provides T2M, T2M_MAX and T2M_MIN in degrees Celsius and PRECTOTCORR in mm/day for 2015–2024, in Local Solar Time. Daily maximum and minimum temperatures drive the FAO-56 Hargreaves calculation of reference evapotranspiration. Published crop coefficients then give estimated crop water use. The app compares that estimate with the entered water depth between turns. It shows historical medians and ranges, the number of complete reference seasons, and a daily audit trail. Precipitation is displayed separately from irrigation supply.

The separate forage case presents an unknown baseline and two sequences from LENSES D2.2 in Deir Alla: sorghum followed by vetch and sesbania followed by barley. The case shows the crop order, seasons, potential soil mechanisms and questions to verify. Exact planting dates and whole-sequence water demand are unavailable. Priorities change which questions appear first. Optional field notes and separate soil ECe and irrigation-water ECw entries are carried into the review, print and audit.

THARA uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap and IBM Plex Sans Arabic. We used Vitest and Playwright for verification, GitHub Pages for hosting, and OpenAI Artifact Tool for the presentation. Claude assisted with planning and initial code. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, calculations, checks, writing and presentation materials. Raw NASA records were retrieved and preserved unchanged. Software-derived estimates, the AI-assisted interface and project mark are disclosed in the app, presentation and metadata.

The intended benefit is a clearer pre-season comparison. POWER provides historical gridded weather. The model excludes effective rainfall, stored soil water and measured field losses. Grower usability, local calibration and actual field outcomes remain unverified.
